known_issues.what: PII rows come from NVIDIA Nemotron-PII (CC-BY-4.0, test split), replacing AI4Privacy. Labels are the source's generated spans, mapped to nine entity types and audited on a 100-document sample (99 confirmed). Every negative passed a screen for gaps the audit found (fax numbers, SSNs on international rows, IPs inside URLs) and a blind AI review.
known_issues.consequence: Driver's licence numbers are not measured: the source has no such label. IP address, password and SSN appear in few test rows, so no per-type claim is made. The negatives' blind review was AI; the project owner later reviewed all current labels.

known_issues.what: All Gandalf rows are mapped to subtask leakage. The source selects instruction-override attempts by embedding similarity and has no per-row leakage label.
known_issues.consequence: Treat as a noisy attack proxy; no leakage-specific claim.

known_issues.what: 32 of 240 selected content test positives map in our taxonomy to PII (21) or TOPIC (11) rather than the five content categories.
known_issues.consequence: Content measures agreement with the sources' policies, not only the five content filters.

known_issues.what: Denied topics and B2 pairs were labelled by a single AI reviewer; each row keeps that origin (label_basis llm, review_status ai_reviewed). On 28 September 2026 the project owner reviewed all current labels in this release and changed none (owner-review-confirmation.json, LABEL_REVIEW.json).
known_issues.consequence: Owner review, not independent two-reviewer adjudication; no inter-rater agreement is measured.

known_issues.what: Profanity rows (civil_comments_obscene) use Civil Comments' crowd-rater obscene share: yes at 0.5 or more, no at 0. 14,800 comments in between and 552 the benchmark had already used were excluded.
known_issues.consequence: Derived binary labels, not unanimous judgments; the hardest borderline cases are absent. For Bedrock's managed profanity filter the score is performance against an external dataset, not identical implementation or vocabulary.

known_issues.what: The 36 lexicon-selected masked-spelling rows (civil_comments_profanity, subtask profanity_obfuscated, AI labels) remain as a diagnostic. The rest of that lexicon-selected set is in release v1.2.
known_issues.consequence: Neither is part of the profanity score.

known_issues.what: B2 has 8 kept pairs: 4 test pairs in 3 groups.
